memoryText: But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read John 20:31 slowly, several times, and say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
John writes these words at the end of his Gospel, and they tell us why he wrote it. It is the key to reading everything else in the book.

“These are written.” The Gospel is a written testimony, chosen from many things Jesus did. John, who saw and heard, put down what we need to know.

“So that you may believe.” The purpose is faith. John does not write only to inform us. He writes to bring us to trust in Jesus.

“That Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God.” Two titles sum up the content of faith: Christ, the promised king and Savior of Israel, and Son of God, the one who shares the nature of the Father. To believe both is to believe the gospel.

“And that by believing.” Faith is the means, not the cause. We are not saved by our faith as a work, but through faith in a person.

“You may have life in his name.” The result is life: forgiveness, new birth, the Spirit, and eternal life, all in the name of Jesus. “In his name” means in the authority and character of his person.

When you wonder what the point of all this reading is, say this verse. It is for you.
weekInReview: This week Jesus taught you to abide in the true vine, because apart from him you can do nothing, and promised the Helper, the Spirit of truth. In the High Priestly Prayer you overheard the Son pray for you, that you would know the only true God, be kept from the evil one, be sanctified by the truth, and be one with his people. You followed Jesus through the garden, the trials before Annas, Caiaphas, and Pilate, and to the cross, where he said “It is finished.” You saw the burial by Joseph and Nicodemus, and the empty tomb. You heard him call Mary by name, watched Thomas confess “My Lord and my God,” and listened as Jesus restored Peter with three questions about love. You finished the Gospel of John and stated its purpose: that you may believe and have life in his name.
reflectionQuestions: Jesus said, “Apart from me you can do nothing.” Where have you been trying to bear fruit on your own, and what would it look like to abide instead?
On the cross, Jesus said, “It is finished.” How does knowing that the work of salvation is complete change the way you live with your guilt and your efforts?
Jesus restored Peter after his denial and gave him a calling. What failure do you need to bring to Jesus, and what would it look like to hear him say “Follow me”?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for the vine, the prayer, the cross, and the empty tomb.
Thank him for writing these things so that you may believe.
